prompt.context: Your client, Acme Cement, is a cement producer in rural New Hampshire. They have one facility where they produce and deliver pre-mixed cement to a range of customers (e.g. building firms) in special trucks designed to stop the cement setting in transit. You have been brought in by the CEO to answer a key question for the company.
prompt.question: Should Acme Cement acquire the neighboring cement producer, which the CEO believes is about to come available, and with whom they have been competing for the last several years?

clarifying_info.q: How far do cement trucks typically travel?
clarifying_info.a: Cement trucks typically only travel within a 2-hour radius before it becomes very costly.
There is one competitor in the area: Cementco.

clarifying_info.q: What is each player's market share?
clarifying_info.a: Acme and Cementco each have 50% market share.
The market for cement and related products is stable but saturated.
Customers are very price sensitive — cement is a commodity product.

clarifying_info.q: What prices do Acme and Cementco charge?
clarifying_info.a: Acme and Cementco charge the same price.

clarifying_info.q: How has Cementco responded to price changes in the past?
clarifying_info.a: Cementco has always responded to Acme's price cuts.
A large majority of customers of both Acme and Cementco are happy with the service they are getting.

framework: Assess the strategic rationale for the acquisition: revenue uplift vs. cost synergies
Evaluate competitive dynamics: what happens if Acme does NOT acquire (who else might buy Cementco)?
Quantify the standalone value of Cementco using DCF (Part B)
Model the incremental value from potential pricing power if Acme achieves monopoly (Part C)
Identify risks: regulatory / antitrust scrutiny, new market entrants triggered by higher prices
Recommend maximum willingness-to-pay and deal structure

questions.prompt: Part A: What should the CEO be thinking about when evaluating this acquisition?
questions.guidance: Candidate should explore both cost and revenue dimensions. On costs: potential synergies (IT, sales, marketing, trucking fleet, support staff) — interviewer should note these are largely negligible given the rural, commodity nature of the business. On revenue: acquiring Cementco removes the only competitor, creating a local monopoly which enables price increases. Candidate should also flag the downside risk of NOT acquiring: an alternative buyer could enter the market and intensify competition. Alternative growth options (new markets, product line expansion, service differentiation, price competition) should be noted but each has significant constraints. The key insight is that the monopoly play is the most compelling strategic rationale.

questions.prompt: Part B: What is the maximum price Acme should pay for Cementco (standalone valuation)?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up a DCF. Cementco generates $2MM in cash flows per year for 10 years. Cost of capital is 10%. The NPV of a 10-year annuity of $2MM at 10% is approximately $12MM. This is the standalone maximum price without considering pricing power. Synergies/economies of scale are negligible.

math.setup: NPV of 10-year annuity: CF = $2MM/year, r = 10%, n = 10 years. NPV = CF × [1 - (1+r)^(-n)] / r
steps: Sum of all 10 PV cash flows ≈ $12.29MM, round to ~$12MM

questions.prompt: Part C: Cementco's owner is asking $24MM. Why might the price be so high, and should Acme pay it?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recognize that acquiring Cementco creates a monopoly, allowing Acme to raise prices. Even a modest $2/ton price increase (3% of $70/ton) applied to 1,400,000 combined tons/year yields $2.8MM in additional annual profit. This incremental cash flow, discounted over 10 years at 10%, adds roughly $17MM to the NPV, pushing total value well above $24MM. Therefore paying $24MM can be justified. Additionally, candidate should discuss risks: (1) antitrust/regulatory blocking of the deal; (2) higher post-merger prices will attract new entrants, eroding the monopoly premium over time. Structuring the payment (e.g., earnout tied to realized price increases) could share risk with the seller and reduce upfront cost.

math.setup: Incremental profit from $2/ton price increase on combined 1.4MM tons/year, then DCF at 10% for 10 years
steps: NPV of incremental profits ≈ $2.8MM × annuity factor(10%, 10yr) ≈ $17.2MM
math.answer: Combined NPV ~$29MM, well above the $24MM ask; buying at $24MM is justified

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential risks and issues the CEO should consider before proceeding with the acquisition at $24MM?

categories.name: Regulatory / Legal
ideas: Antitrust review — local monopoly may trigger regulatory scrutiny or blocking

categories.name: Competitive Response
ideas: High post-merger prices will attract new entrants into the NH cement market
New entrant could build or acquire a facility, eroding monopoly pricing power
Geographic isolation (2-hour radius) provides some natural barrier but not absolute

categories.name: Deal Structure / Financing
ideas: Earnout structure tied to realized price increases shares risk with seller
Upfront price of $24MM requires significant capital; assess financing cost vs. value creation
Overpayment risk if pricing power proves harder to realize than modeled

categories.name: Operational
ideas: Trucking fleet rationalization could provide small synergy not captured in base model

categories.name: Market Risk
ideas: Market is stable but saturated — volume growth unlikely to offset if prices cannot be raised
Customer defection risk if prices increase significantly

recommendation: Acme should acquire Cementco at up to ~$24MM, justified by the monopoly pricing power that would result from becoming the sole cement producer in the local market
A $2/ton price increase on 1.4MM combined tons generates ~$2.8MM in additional annual profit, pushing total NPV to ~$29MM — above the $24MM asking price
risks: Antitrust/regulatory scrutiny could block the deal or require divestitures
Higher post-acquisition prices will incentivize new competitors to enter the market, eroding the monopoly premium over time
next_steps: Conduct antitrust pre-clearance assessment before committing
Explore deal structuring options (earnout, deferred payments) to share pricing risk with the seller
Model sensitivity of NPV to new entrant scenarios and timeline
If deal proceeds, develop a phased pricing strategy to test customer elasticity before full price increases
